tagline.text: A roughly 70 m waterfall below the Batad rice terraces

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: December–June dry season (green planting in April–May)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,500–2,500 (day trip from Banaue, guide and transport included, small group)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL), about 9–10 hours by road

children.text: Tappiya Falls is a roughly 70 m waterfall hidden below the UNESCO-listed Batad rice terraces. The walk from the village takes 1–1.5 hours on steep paths, but the cold pool and spray at the end of the terraces and stairs repay the effort.

Tappiya Falls (also spelled Tappiyah or Tappia) lies near the village of Batad in Banaue, Ifugao, in the Cordillera mountains of northern Luzon. Batad is famous for rice terraces that curve around the hillside like an amphitheater, and if you walk down through them, a waterfall drops into the valley below the village. It is described as about 230 feet, or about 70 m, high, with a pool at its base that can be used for swimming.

The route to the falls is half of the trip. From Batad village you walk along narrow paddy walls, up and down stone steps, and sometimes past muddy paths and flooded paddies. One travel blog puts it at about 1–1.5 hours each way at a moderate fitness level, while also calling it far from easy. The return climb includes steep, uneven steps with risers often nearly a foot high, and many visitors say the way back is harder than the way down.

Batad itself is a mountain village that no cars can enter, so everything is on foot. From Banaue town you take a jeepney or tricycle up to the saddle, then walk a short trail into the village. That is why many travelers do not turn back the same day after seeing just the falls, but stay a night in Batad and combine a sunrise view of the terraces with the falls trek.

You can swim in the pool, but one visitor review says that after a typhoon in November 2025 large rocks and mud filled the pool, making swimming difficult and leaving room only to dip your feet. This guide compares several blogs and map sources, and some details are old, so check the current situation with the Banaue tourism office and a village guide before you go. You will be less disappointed if your goal is to walk down and feel the spray rather than to swim.

The falls hide at the very bottom of the terraces and are described as about 230 feet (about 70 m) high. One blogger photographed them from the roof of a shelter about 100 feet above the falls. After heavy rain the flow increases and the spray reaches far.

The path itself is a highlight. It follows narrow walls between rice terraces, and the view changes with every step. In some places one side is a shallow muddy paddy and the other drops about 10 feet (about 3 m), so watch your footing.

The pool below the falls is very cold and refreshing after the walk. Recent reviews say large rocks and mud have made swimming difficult at times, so ask your guide about the current condition before deciding to swim.

In Batad, local residents work as guides and tell stories of the village and the history of the terraces as well as showing you the falls. Guide fees become village income, so hiring a local guide is the responsible way to travel.
The falls trek is usually combined with the viewpoint above the village (Top View) in one day. Guide fee lists also treat the viewpoint and Tappiya Falls as one package.
Staying in a traditional Ifugao house in the village brings you closer to local culture through dinner and conversation. Lodging is mostly simple but warm.

blocks.title: Quiet photos on the way down

children.text: The terraces look completely different in early morning mist and late-afternoon light, and some people walk the same path twice. The trip takes long, so leave plenty of time for photos.
Have breakfast at your Batad lodging and prepare water, snacks and a walking stick. Confirm the route and fee with your guide.
Leave the village and follow the paddy walls down toward the falls. A walking stick is almost essential, and you can easily borrow one from your lodging or guide.
Take photos of the whole waterfall from the viewpoint and shelter. If you are fit, continue down to the pool.
Rest in the spray at the pool. Decide whether to swim based on its condition.
The climb back is a steep stone staircase, so go slowly and rest. Allow about 1.5 hours for the return.
Have lunch and rest at a restaurant in the village.
Be sure to return to the village before dark. Walking stairs and paddy walls after dark is dangerous.
Take a jeepney or tricycle from Banaue to the saddle, then walk into Batad village.
Look down over the whole terrace amphitheater from the viewpoint above the village.
Go early for the Tappiya Falls trek.
Time your return to the saddle with the jeepney and head back to Banaue.
Take an overnight bus from Manila to Banaue. Ohayami Transit and Dangwa Transit (Florida) and others leave around 8:00 PM, with a fare of about ₱900 and a travel time of about 8–10 hours.
The Coda Lines overnight bus to Sagada also passes through Banaue.
Schedules and fares change, so check the latest announcements.
Reaching Batad from Manila in a single day is hard. Plan to stay a night in Banaue or arrive at dawn and continue.

items.title: From Banaue to the Batad saddle

children.text: The Batad saddle is about 18 km from Banaue town, about 45 minutes by jeepney.
The direct jeepney runs once or twice a day (usually at 3:00 PM, and also at 9:00 AM in summer) and the fare is reported at about ₱150. Some of this information is old, so confirm locally.
A tricycle is reported at about ₱400 for 2–3 people, or about ₱300 to the saddle only. Chartering a jeepney starts at around ₱1,500.

The shared jeepney from Batad back to Banaue is usually a single trip at 9:00 AM, so missing it is a problem. If you miss it, walk about 6 km to Batad Junction and flag down a tricycle or jeepney, or charter a vehicle at the saddle.
Confirm the shared jeepney schedule locally in Banaue the day before. Service may be reduced or added depending on the season and number of passengers.

items.title: From the saddle to the village and falls

children.text: The village is about 500 m from the saddle, about a 15-minute walk.
From the village to Tappiya Falls is about 1–1.5 hours each way on foot. Use a walking stick and go with a village guide.
The dry season from December to June is easier for walking, and in April–May the freshly planted terraces are at their greenest. In July–August the rice ripens to gold.

In the rainy season the risk of landslides, falling rocks and slippery mud rises. After a typhoon, rocks and mud can fill the pool and make swimming difficult, so check the current condition before you arrive.
It is ideal to start the trek around 8:00 AM. The midday sun is strong, and in the afternoon fog or rain can make the return dangerous.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: The most comfortable time to trek, and the pool is very cold
Green planting (April–May) and sunrise views are beautiful
Paths are slippery and rockfall is a risk, so leave extra time in your plan

Batad has no hotels or resorts, just converted family homes and guesthouses. The cheapest places cost around ₱250 per person, and you can even sleep in a traditional Ifugao hut. Lodgings are spread across the upper and lower parts of the village, so pack light.

Meals are at your lodging or small restaurants in the village. You can try the traditional Ifugao dish pinikpikan and local rice wine. There are no ATMs or card payments in the village and the mobile signal is weak, so bring plenty of cash.

Staying overnight in Batad is much easier on your body. You can leave early, reach the falls before the midday heat and rest in the village in the afternoon. A day trip from Banaue, on the other hand, leaves little time at the falls because of the jeepney schedule. Some lodgings can also arrange a guide, so ask when you book.
Bring or borrow a walking stick. It protects your knees a lot on stairs and muddy paths.
Start early. One review says a 3:00 PM start left only a few minutes at the falls.
Calculate your return before sunset. Allow about 1.5 hours for the way back.
Wear trekking shoes or shoes with good grip. Sandals are dangerous.
Carry enough cash, water and snacks. There is only one store near the falls.
If you want to swim, bring a change of clothes and a towel. Ask your guide about the pool's condition first.
Walk in single file on the paddy walls and do not step on or pick the rice.
Mobile signal is weak, so prepare an offline map and contact numbers in advance.
When you reach Banaue, register first at the tourism office, pay the environmental fee and ask for a licensed guide. Batad has many guides, so you can also find one on the spot.
Guide fees depend on the route and group size, so settle what is included and the price before you start. Older posts range from ₱400 to ₱1,500, a wide spread.
After rain the paddy walls and stairs are very slippery, and falling rocks sometimes fill the pool. Make sure you are back before dark.
Some paddy walls are narrow, with a drop of about 3 m on one side, so keep your balance.
The stone steps on the way back are high and hard on the knees. Climb slowly with rests.
Fees, guides and transport change from year to year, so check the latest information at the Banaue tourism office.
Right after a typhoon or rockfall the trail and pool may have changed, so follow your guide's judgment.
Never hike down in the dark. Even with a flashlight it is dangerous.
The amphitheater-shaped terraces in the same village as the falls, with the whole view from the viewpoint.
